options.name: Vashti Skiles Community Center (Langtry)
options.priceNote: Free / suggested $2-5 donation via iron-ranger box
options.locationNote: Torres Ave, right in Langtry, 2 blocks from the Judge Roy Bean Visitor Center; coordinates approximate
options.legalityNote: Community-sanctioned overnight area (former school lot with donation box) - the long-running Langtry cyclist camp tradition continues here; no restrooms on site
options.cyclistIntel: Southern Tier tradition of camping behind the Langtry community center is intact; Campendium reviews through Mar 2025 confirm overnights welcomed (quiet, level gravel, good 5G). Fill ALL bottles at the Judge Roy Bean Visitor Center (drinking water, flush restrooms, AC lobby, open 8-5 daily) BEFORE 5pm - there is no store, gas station, or other water in town. Local dogs bark at night per Mar 2025 review.
options.seasonalNote: Visitor center was under construction in 2025 but lobby/restrooms stayed open 8-5 daily; call TxDOT center (432-291-3340) to confirm water access

options.name: Seminole Canyon State Park (Desert Vista / Roadrunner Flat primitive)
options.priceNote: $10/night primitive site + $4/person daily entrance; sites with water $15 + $4
options.locationNote: Park HQ off US 90, ~19 mi before Langtry; primitive areas a short ride inside the park
options.legalityNote: TPWD state park - fully legal, reservable on Texas State Parks system
options.cyclistIntel: The guaranteed option: potable water, restrooms with showers near the main loop, shade shelters at water sites. If Langtry feels sketchy on arrival day, shorten the day and stop here; next water is Langtry visitor center (8-5 only).
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; October is prime season - reserve the $15 water sites online, primitive usually has space

gapAdvice: Arrive in Langtry before 5pm to load water at the visitor center. If the community center situation has changed, backtrack is impossible - so if in doubt, commit to Seminole Canyon (mile 1398.5) instead and ride a longer Day 25.

options.name: Terrell County Visitor Center / picnic area grounds
options.locationNote: 108 E Oak St, downtown Sanderson, one block off US 90; coordinates approximate
options.legalityNote: County-welcomed cyclist camping outside the community center/visitor center - a documented Southern Tier institution
options.cyclistIntel: David Helder's Southern Tier notes: 'camp outside the community center; nice restrooms at the visitor center; water and WiFi always available.' Official county hours are now Wed-Sat 12-5 (Oct 15 2026 is a Thursday - open). Call ahead to confirm camping is still welcomed and where they want your tent.
options.seasonalNote: Hours reduced vs the old 8-5; outdoor water spigot historically available even when closed - verify by phone

options.name: Canyons RV Park
options.priceNote: $7 tent + $3 shower per recent reviews - call to confirm current rate
options.locationNote: US 90, east side of Sanderson, 0.1 mi off route
options.legalityNote: Established commercial RV park, tents explicitly accepted
options.cyclistIntel: Covered tenting pavilion with lights and electricity - huge in wind or rain. At $7+$3 shower this may beat the free option after 60 desert miles. Open year-round with full hookups, laundry, WiFi.

bestBet: Terrell County Visitor Center / picnic area grounds
gapAdvice: Budget Inn Sanderson (US 90 west side, ~$55-70) is the cheap roof fallback. Sanderson has a grocery (Stripes/Family Dollar) - resupply here, the next 71 mi to Marathon are empty.

options.name: Post Park (Fort Pena Colorado County Park)
options.locationNote: 5 mi south of Marathon at the south end of Avenue D / Post Rd - 5 mi OFF route each way
options.legalityNote: Brewster County park; camping explicitly allowed on the east side of the spring-fed pond (pack out trash)
options.cyclistIntel: Restrooms open 24/7, picnic tables, grills, cottonwood shade, spring pond (not potable - carry water from town). Lovely but adds 10 hilly bonus miles; only worth it if the in-town options fail.
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; occasional community events use the park

options.name: Marathon Motel & RV Park
options.priceNote: $15/night tent per reviews - confirm by phone; motel/RV park confirms camping area on site
options.locationNote: US 90 at the west end of Marathon, on route as you leave town westbound
options.legalityNote: Established motel + RV park with dedicated tent camping behind the property
options.cyclistIntel: Flat tent pads, picnic tables, clean restrooms/showers, laundry, and nightly stargazing with telescopes (certified dark-sky country). Reliable, easy, on route.

options.name: La Loma del Chivo hostel
options.priceNote: ~$20-25/night; long-standing tradition of cyclists' first night FREE if no paying guests - confirm when you call
options.locationNote: 401 SW 6th St, a few blocks south of US 90 in Marathon; coordinates approximate - anyone in town can point you
options.legalityNote: Private hostel property - fully legal, famously quirky (papercrete buildings, resident goats)
options.cyclistIntel: THE legendary Southern Tier cyclist stop in Marathon - beds in eccentric handmade structures plus tent space, kitchen, showers. Active listings on Yelp (Dec 2025) and booking.com indicate still operating; reviews are polarizing (rustic/eccentric), so know what you're getting.
options.seasonalNote: Appears operating as of late 2025 - call to verify before relying on it

gapAdvice: Gage Gardens is a private hotel garden - no camping. If La Loma is full/closed, Marathon Motel's $15 tent sites are the sure thing.

options.name: Tumble In RV Park
options.priceNote: $15/person tent (verified on official rates page); $25 for two
options.locationNote: US 90 at the east edge of Marfa, ~1.5 mi before downtown - you pass it riding in; coordinates approximate
options.legalityNote: Commercial RV park; tent camping first-come first-served (can pre-pay online but sites not reserved)
options.cyclistIntel: Tent campers get access to all park facilities (restrooms/showers on site). Self-service vibe. Exposed and windy - stake well. NOTE: El Cosmico, the famous Marfa campground, has CLOSED its original site (relocating as 'El Cosmico 2.0') - do not plan on it.
options.seasonalNote: Marfa fills up during events (Chinati Weekend is usually early-to-mid Oct) - arrive early to claim a tent spot

options.name: Lost Alaskan RV Park (Alpine - 26 mi before Marfa)
options.priceNote: ~$25-40; covered tent areas with electric; $40 full-site rate reported Oct 2024 - call for tent rate
options.locationNote: 2401 N Hwy 118, Alpine - about 1.8 mi north of the US 90 route through Alpine
options.legalityNote: Established commercial RV park with 8 dedicated covered tent sites (12x12 gravel pads, electric, picnic table)
options.cyclistIntel: Use this if you want to split the day shorter and stay in Alpine (full grocery, bike shop, restaurants - the best resupply between Del Rio and El Paso). No online booking - phone only.

options.name: Rancho Estrella Marfa (Hipcamp)
options.priceNote: Rate not published in listing preview - check Hipcamp; area listings average $20-35
options.locationNote: Edge of Marfa, ~0.5-1 mi walk to downtown; coordinates approximate
options.legalityNote: Legal private-land camping booked through Hipcamp (tent sites around a 100-year-old adobe church)
options.cyclistIntel: Toilet, potable water, showers, WiFi, picnic tables listed; currently bookable. Good backup if Tumble In is slammed for an event weekend.

options.name: Paisano Baptist Encampment
options.priceNote: Unknown - historic church campground; fee/donation possible if they host you at all
options.locationNote: 91872 US Hwy 90 at Paisano Pass, between Alpine and Marfa; coordinates approximate
options.legalityNote: Private Baptist encampment grounds - ONLY with advance permission; no documented cyclist-hosting tradition found
options.cyclistIntel: Century-old cowboy camp-meeting grounds with tabernacle and cabins, right on route at the pass. Summer meeting is July; grounds likely quiet in October. Contact via their website well ahead - do not just show up.
options.seasonalNote: Main encampment event is in July; off-season access unverified

gapAdvice: The OSM 'Dispersed Camping Marfa' node at mile 1597.9 could not be verified as legal camping - likely an informal roadside pullout; skip it. El Cosmico is closed. If everything in Marfa is full (event weekend), Alpine at mile 1581 is the pressure valve.

options.name: Valentine School grounds (with permission)
options.priceNote: Free with permission from school staff/principal
options.locationNote: Valentine ISD school on US 90 in town (pop ~130); day marker mile 1647.2 sits ~4 mi NW of town - camp in town
options.legalityNote: Permission-based only: a 2023 Southern Tier journal documents the principal allowing cyclists to camp on school grounds and use the bathrooms. Ask first - never set up unannounced at a school.
options.cyclistIntel: Crazyguyonabike 2023 ('Pedaling Through the Southern Tier', Day 34 Van Horn to Valentine) camped here with staff permission and bathroom access. Arrive during school hours (before ~4pm) to ask; a weekend/holiday arrival makes this much harder. Oct 18 2026 is a SUNDAY - school will be closed, so call Valentine ISD the Friday before, or ask at the post office/any local.
options.seasonalNote: School closed Sundays - arrange by phone in advance for an Oct 18 arrival

options.name: Love Shaks (Airbnb vintage trailers)
options.priceNote: ~$80-120/night estimated - over budget, but the only roofed option; owner has waived the 2-night minimum for passing cyclists
options.locationNote: Vintage trailers in Valentine proper; find via Airbnb search 'Valentine TX'
options.cyclistIntel: The 2023 CGOAB journal reports the Love Shaks owner waived the two-night minimum for cyclists passing through - message the host ahead explaining you're a Southern Tier rider.
options.seasonalNote: Book several days ahead; inventory is tiny

gapAdvice: Valentine has NO motel, store, or restaurant - carry dinner/breakfast and full water from Marfa. Sunday arrival means arrange school permission by phone Friday, or knock at the church/post office - locals are used to Southern Tier riders. Prada Marfa (mile ~1645) is an art installation, not a campsite. Fallbacks: book a Love Shak, backtrack nothing (Marfa is 36 mi behind), or grind 38 more mi to Van Horn RV Park - not recommended after a 40-mi day.

options.name: Sierra Blanca Public Park
options.locationNote: Middle of Sierra Blanca, off the I-10 business loop; coordinates approximate
options.legalityNote: Public town park; iOverlander reviews report locals confirm overnighting is allowed (mostly RV reports - a tent is more visible, so confirm with the sheriff's office or any local when you arrive)
options.cyclistIntel: Bathrooms and dumpsters at the park, town amenities (gas station food, Delfina's/cafe, small stores) walkable. Sierra Blanca is a Border Patrol town - checking in with a local or deputy buys you a peaceful night. Carry water in from Van Horn; park spigot unverified.
options.seasonalNote: Fine in October; nights get cold at 4,500 ft

options.name: Van Horn RV Park (35 mi before, shortened-day option)
options.priceNote: Tent rate not published; typical $20-25 - call 432-283-2728
options.locationNote: 10 Kampers Lane, east side of Van Horn off the I-10 frontage (exact GPS from park website)
options.legalityNote: Commercial RV park with 8 dedicated tent-only sites
options.cyclistIntel: Tent sites have electric, water, picnic tables, BBQ grills; store, cafe (Penny's Cafe opens Oct 1 - perfect timing), laundry, restrooms and showers steps away. Van Horn is the last full-service town before El Paso; if the Valentine night went badly, stop short here and re-split the days.
options.seasonalNote: Penny's Cafe on site operates Oct 1 - Apr 30

options.name: Mountain View RV Park (Van Horn)
options.priceNote: Estimated $15-25; large park listed as accepting tents - call to confirm
options.locationNote: Van Horn, off Business I-10/Broadway; coordinates approximate - confirm location on arrival
options.legalityNote: Commercial RV park listed as accepting tents (200 sites)
options.cyclistIntel: Backup to Van Horn RV Park; Van Horn also has cheap motels ($45-60) if weather turns.

gapAdvice: No RV park in Sierra Blanca itself takes tents (nothing verified operating). If the public park feels wrong, Sierra Blanca has budget motels (Americana Inn, ~$50-60). Load ALL water in Van Horn - the 35 mi between have zero services, and the I-10 frontage climb is exposed.

options.name: Fort Hancock Community Church (18 mi before Fabens)
options.priceNote: Free with permission - donations to the church appreciated
options.locationNote: Fort Hancock town center off US 80/route; ask anyone in town for the community church; coordinates approximate
options.legalityNote: Permission-based church-yard camping - a documented Southern Tier cyclist stop (multiple journal accounts, incl. German riders Felix Greiner & Jenny Prasiswa camped at the church)
options.cyclistIntel: Fort Hancock is described in journals as 'a cyclist's oasis' - famously hospitable. Gas station/convenience store and a cash-only restaurant in town; Fort Hancock Motel (~$60-70) as backup. Recent (2024-26) confirmations are thin - call the Hudspeth County sheriff's Fort Hancock substation or knock early.

options.name: Cotton Valley Travel Center / RV parking (past Fabens)
options.priceNote: Unverified - likely truck-stop style RV parking; tent policy unknown, call/ask on arrival
options.locationNote: ~7 route miles past Fabens toward Clint/San Elizario, ~3 mi off route near I-10; coordinates very approximate
options.legalityNote: Could NOT be verified as a tent-legal campground - treat as a services stop, not a planned campsite
options.cyclistIntel: Appears in OSM as a travel center; no tent-camping evidence found in any source. Only useful for water/food or paid overnight RV-lot parking if they allow it.

bestBet: Fort Hancock Community Church (18 mi before Fabens)
gapAdvice: Fabens itself has NO verified legal camping - this is the segment's real gap. Best plays: (1) shorten the day and camp at Fort Hancock Community Church (mile ~1772) with permission - the established cyclist move; (2) take a roof night: Fabens Inn, 1884 Fabens Rd near I-10, ~$79/night (reviews warn of surprise fees - confirm total price at check-in), or Fort Hancock Motel ~$60-70; (3) push ~20 more miles into El Paso's Mission Valley where motels are plentiful. Do not stealth camp in the irrigated farm strip - it is all private land near the border with heavy Border Patrol presence.
